findings.finding: The SEK 244m adj EBIT bar implies a Q2-to-Q3 drop of SEK 275m (519 to 244). That is bigger than 2025's 257m drop (454 to 197), and the 2025 quarter carried an extended maintenance stop at one of the largest Sandviken units, which took Tube's adj EBIT to SEK 101m (202). On top of that, Q3 2026 carries roughly SEK 50m of y/y savings from measures begun in October 2025 and a neutral FX effect y/y, so the comp looks easy enough that the bar is modestly beatable, even net of the guided tube-mill ramp-up costs.

Beats have mostly been bought, but not always.

findings.why_not_priced: The bar was published only on 2026-10-23 and implies just 5.6% margin, below the 7.0% of Q3 2024. If the market priced a clear beat, the stock would not have given back about 6% over 20 sessions (118.9 to 112.1, mostly with the OMX), and the 1.81% short is static, not covering. Four to seven analysts and $1.7m a day of turnover put this in the under-read band. Against that, analysts can do the same arithmetic, and the guided ramp-up costs are an unquantified offset.
findings.independence: Same company documents, so not fully independent. The Q2 2026 report's own Q3 outlook (https://attachment.news.eu.nasdaq.com/a43c2a648673d7b77caa4f29f085651bf) speaks only of normal seasonal maintenance, not an extended stop, and gives neutral FX y/y.

findings.finding: Swedish engineering counterparties that reported this week showed short-cycle general industry improving. Sandvik Machining's organic orders rose 33%, Europe +31% ('improved sentiment in general industry'), and October cutting-tool daily orders were stable vs Q3; Atlas Copco's organic orders rose 25%; SKF grew 4.3% organically with EMEA broadly unchanged. That points to Alleima's weakest short-cycle Industrial segment having stabilised in Q3 orders.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Order intake and segment demand arrows drive the reaction here. The Q2 2026 report headlined 'improved order intake' and the stock rose 5.4%; the Q4 2025 report saw continued weak short-cycle demand and the stock fell 11.2%.
findings.why_not_priced: ALLEI fell 2.3% on 2026-10-22, the day Sandvik and Atlas Copco reported, moving with the OMXS30 (-2.5%), so the read-through was not credited to it. A priced read-through would show ALLEI outperforming the index over 10/21-10/23, and it did not. This is a proxy: Sandvik's growth is partly tungsten prices and customer pre-buying, SKF's EMEA was flat, and Alleima's Chemical and Petrochemical demand is investment-driven, not short-cycle.
